title: French: 500 Most Common Words

sources.name: Original educational synthesis from general knowledge

description: For beginners: 500 common French words in approximate frequency order, with noun gender and original examples. Latin-script headwords also serve as romanization; ranks vary by corpus.

cards.back: un — a; one (masculine article or numeral)
une — a; one (feminine article or numeral)
qui — who; which (relative or interrogative pronoun)
ne — negative particle, usually paired with pas
en — in; by; some; of it (preposition or pronoun)
que — that; what; whom (conjunction or pronoun)
du — of the; some (masculine article contraction)

cards.example: Le chat est sur la table.

cards.back: ils — they (masculine or mixed plural pronoun)
son — his; her; its (possessive determiner before masculine singular nouns)
sa — his; her; its (possessive determiner before feminine singular nouns)
ses — his; her; its (plural possessive determiner)
au — to the; at the (à + le)
aux — to the; at the (à + les)
plus — more; no more in ne...plus (adverb)
lui — him; her; to him; to her (pronoun)
leur — their; to them (determiner or pronoun)
mon — my (possessive determiner before masculine singular nouns)
ma — my (possessive determiner before feminine singular nouns)
te — you; yourself (informal singular object pronoun)
votre — your (formal or plural possessor; singular possessed noun)
vos — your (formal or plural possessor; plural possessed noun)
pouvoir — to be able to; can (verb)
savoir — to know a fact; to know how (verb)
devoir — to have to; must; to owe (verb)
rien — nothing; anything in negative contexts (pronoun)

cards.example: Le banc est entre les arbres.
Je bois du thé sans sucre.

cards.back: chez — at the home of; at the business of (preposition)

cards.example: Le chien est sous la table.
Je vis ici depuis un an.
Le vélo est contre le mur.

cards.back: gens — people (plural noun, usually masculine agreement)
passer — to pass; to spend time (verb)

cards.example: Tu peux laisser ton sac ici.

cards.back: regarder — to look at; to watch (verb)
sortir — to go out; to leave (verb)
connaître — to know; to be acquainted with (verb)

cards.example: Les plantes peuvent mourir sans eau.

cards.back: marcher — to walk; to work mechanically (verb)

cards.example: Il ne faut pas oublier les clés.
Je ne veux pas perdre ce billet.

cards.back: rendre — to give back; to make (verb)
poser — to put down; to ask a question (verb)
reprendre — to resume; to take again (verb)
retourner — to return; to turn over (verb)

cards.example: Ce dessin peut représenter un arbre.

cards.back: remettre — to put back; to hand over (verb)
cards.example: Il faut remettre la chaise ici.

cards.back: dont — whose; of which; of whom (relative pronoun)
cards.example: Voici le livre dont je parle.
Le bureau est près de la fenêtre.
Le corps a besoin de repos.

cards.back: cheveu — hair; a strand of hair (masculine noun)
cards.example: Un cheveu est sur la veste.

cards.back: professeur — teacher; professor (masculine or feminine noun)
élève — pupil; student (masculine or feminine noun)
chef — head; leader; chef (masculine or feminine noun)

cards.example: Je reste car je suis fatigué.

cards.back: information — information; piece of information (feminine noun)
nouvelle — news item; short story (feminine noun)

cards.example: Le fromage est sur la table.
Je prends du thé sans sucre.
Le chat est derrière le lit.
Il y a sept jours dans une semaine.
Le magasin ouvre à huit heures.
La ville est à mille kilomètres.
La route est en bon état.
Il est au milieu du jardin.
La table a une forme ronde.

cards.back: mal — badly; pain (adverb or masculine noun)

cards.example: Tu as le droit de partir.
